name: BaqFlo SamePage
author: baqflo

sections.description:
BaqFlo SamePage turns ordinary WordPress content into clear, smooth navigation without requiring you to manually create and maintain anchor IDs.

Choose the headings, sections, classes, or IDs SamePage should discover. The plugin creates stable hidden anchors before those elements, then makes the resulting links available in WordPress menus and directly inside the block editor.

Link to sections across your website

SamePage’s SP Link toolbar button is not limited to the page you are editing. Search indexed pages, posts, and products, choose a section, and insert the complete cross-page URL automatically.

This makes SamePage especially useful for documentation, guides, service pages, product information, FAQs, and any website where related sections need to be connected clearly.

Core features

  • Automatically discovers headings and other configured page elements.
  • Creates stable hidden anchors without overwriting IDs supplied by your theme or page builder.
  • Adds SamePage sections to Appearance > Menus.
  • Includes a Gutenberg SP Link button for current-page and cross-page section links.
  • Searches site-wide destinations by entering / in the SP Link picker.
  • Supports pages, posts, and WooCommerce products.
  • Lets editors choose which content appears in the SamePage link index.
  • Rebuilds the site-wide link index from the SamePage dashboard.
  • Smoothly scrolls to linked sections with configurable speed.
  • Adds BFSP-active and BFSP-inactive classes as visitors move through the page.
  • Keeps standard browser hash-link fallback when JavaScript is unavailable.
  • Supports comma-separated element, class, and ID selectors.
  • Avoids opinionated menu styling so links continue to match the active theme.

SamePage Pro

SamePage Pro adds advanced navigation generation and behaviour, including automatic navigation widgets, named auto-included sections, sticky-header intelligence, parent-menu highlighting, mobile-menu handling, Back to Top controls, and clean URL options.

Learn more at baqflo.com/samepage/.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate BaqFlo SamePage.
  2. Open Appearance > Customize > BaqFlo – SamePage and choose the selectors SamePage should discover.
  3. Edit a page, post, or product and enable Include in SamePage Links in its SamePage settings panel.
  4. Update the content so its anchors are indexed.
  5. Add discovered sections through Appearance > Menus > SamePage Links, or use the SP Link button in the block editor.
  6. Use BaqFlo > SamePage > Rebuild Link Index after broad content changes when you want to refresh all indexed destinations at once.
sections.faq:
Does SamePage overwrite existing element IDs?

No. SamePage inserts a hidden, non-layout anchor marker before a discovered element instead of replacing IDs created by WordPress, your theme, or a page builder.

Can I link to a section on another page?

Yes. Select text in the block editor, open SP Link, enter / to browse indexed content, select a page, then choose its destination section. SamePage inserts the complete page URL and anchor.

Which selectors are supported?

SamePage supports comma-separated element, class, and ID selectors such as h2, h3, section, .feature-heading, and #pricing.

Why is a page missing from SamePage Links?

Edit that page, post, or product, enable Include in SamePage Links in the SamePage settings panel, and update the content. You can also use Rebuild Link Index from the SamePage dashboard.

Do links work without JavaScript?

Yes. SamePage uses normal anchor URLs, so the browser’s standard hash-link behaviour remains available.

Does SamePage style my menu?

No. SamePage adds navigation-state classes but leaves visual styling to your active theme or custom CSS.
sections.changelog:
1.02

  • Replaced legacy generic shortcode tags in stored content with the product-specific baqflo_sp_anchor shortcode.
  • Removed registration of the legacy samepage_anchor and bfsp_anchor shortcode aliases.
  • Restored clean-link navigation for Pro-authored aliases after downgrading to Lite, without exposing clean-link creation controls.
  • Improved clean-hash resolution for page loads and menu clicks, including compatibility metadata and case-insensitive matching.

1.01

  • Preserved existing Pro-authored clean anchor links after an intentional downgrade, including links whose saved compatibility metadata was removed by an earlier Lite render; Lite does not create or manage clean aliases.
  • Added plugin-specific technical identifiers and a non-destructive migration for existing SamePage settings, page selections, anchor registries, and navigation assignments.
  • Preserved existing BFSP anchor IDs, public CSS classes, and previously created links.
  • Added the BaqFlo dashboard integration and refreshed SamePage documentation links.
  • Improved compatibility and removed PHP warnings during automatic anchor generation.

1.00

  • Initial WordPress.org release.

screenshots.caption: Getenberg integration - SP Link button: Create SamePage links directly inside the editor without manually searching for anchor names.  SP Link button also supports links between pages. Enter / in the search box to browse pages containing SamePage anchors, then select the section you want to link to.
SamePage settings can be found in Customizer, and include element/selector options for auto-anchor creation, scroll speed, and overriding navigation active state.
SamePage Links are automatically included in the WordPress menu builder.  Choose the SamePage enabled content, and add the SamePage anchors just like standard menu items.

(PRO VERSION) Display page-specific navigation in sidebars, documentation layouts, landing pages, and content hubs. Pro also features SamePage anchor blocks. Create navigation exactly where it belongs. Drop a SamePage Anchor block anywhere in your content, give it a title, and SamePage automatically adds it to your page navigation. Drag anchors to reorder sections, duplicate them when needed, and even create nested navigation by adding -- before a title to generate child menu items automatically. This makes building documentation, tutorials, landing pages, and long-form content navigation incredibly fast and visual.
